newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand downplays concerns on short-term debt.
newsitem.headline: Thailand downplays concerns on short-term debt.

text.p: Thailand's central bank on Tuesday downplayed concerns about short-term foreign debt and said short-term external borrowings by local borrowers through its offshore banking facility had declined sharply last year.

The Bank of Thailand said foreign borrowings made through the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF) with maturity of more than one year accounted for 34.2 percent of total foreign borrowings at the end of 1996 compared with only 9.4 percent at the end of January, 1996.
"Some analysts had expressed concern that foreign borrowings through the BIBF had too short (a) maturity," the Bank of Thailand said in a statement.
The level of short-term foreign borrowings had now declined, it added.
Foreign borrowings with maturity of one year and less fell to 65.8 percent of the total at the end of 1996 from 90.6 percent at the end of January 1996, it added.
At the end of 1996, total foreign borrowings through the BIBF was 807 billion baht ($31 billion), it said.
Most of the long-term foreign borrowings had maturity of between three and five years, the central bank said.
